terms.latin: dē imprōvīsō opprimō, opprimere, oppressī, oppressum
terms.gloss: come on someone unexpectedly, take by surprise
evidence: Hirt. B.G. 8.36.3: dē imprōvīsō (Lewis & Short, s.v. imprūdēns)
terms.comment: Opprimere is “to fall on, overwhelm”; with dē imprōvīsō or ex imprōvīsō (“unexpectedly”) it is to catch someone off guard. To surprise someone with a present is dē imprōvīsō dōnāre.
Morgan–Owens’ phrase, from Terence: the person caught is imprūdēns, “not expecting it”.
Catching someone doing something, found out.

phrases.latin: Dē imprōvīsō tē opprimam. … Tē nec opīnantem oppresserō.
phrases.english: I’ll take you by surprise. … I’ll pounce on you when you least expect it.
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Fōrmulae, Invītandī ad convīvium

phrases.latin: nē dē hāc rē pater inprūdentem opprimat
phrases.english: so that my father doesn’t catch him unawares with this business
